stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Drag the three sliders and watch two views react: on top, the AM waveform $s(t) = [1 + m\cos(2\pi f_m t)]\cos(2\pi f_p t)$ with its envelope in amber; on the bottom, the spectrum — a carrier line at $f_p$ flanked by two sidebands at $f_p \pm f_m$. Push the modulation index $m$ past $1$ to witness over-modulation. Advance after using every slider and once witnessing $m > 1$.
stages.concept: Amplitude modulation packages a low-frequency message $u(t)$ onto a high-frequency carrier $p(t) = \cos(2\pi f_p t)$ by scaling its amplitude: $s(t) = [1 + m\cos(2\pi f_m t)]\cos(2\pi f_p t)$. Three parameters: message frequency $f_m$, carrier frequency $f_p \gg f_m$, and modulation index $m$. The envelope traces $1 + m\cos(2\pi f_m t)$; a receiver recovers the message by tracking that envelope. In the frequency domain the multiplication becomes convolution: the message spectrum (a single line at $f_m$) is copied to $f_p - f_m$ and $f_p + f_m$ around the carrier. That's why AM bandwidth is $2 f_m$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Each target locks in a specific $(f_m, f_p, m)$. Tune your sliders so the solid teal signal matches the dashed grey target curve. Both plots update live — use the spectrum lines as landmarks. Tolerance: $\pm 5\%$ on frequencies, $\pm 0.05$ on $m$.
stages.concept: Reading AM by eye: the number of envelope bumps in the window tells you $f_m$; the density of fast oscillations under the envelope tells you $f_p$; the envelope depth (peak vs. trough) tells you $m$. When $m = 1$ the envelope just touches zero — that's critical modulation, the sweet spot before distortion.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The waveform is hidden. From the spectrum alone — three vertical lines with their frequencies labeled — deduce $f_p$, $f_m$, and $m$. Read $f_p$ from the tall middle line; $f_m$ is half the sideband spacing; $m$ is twice the sideband-to-carrier amplitude ratio. Peek briefly re-shows the waveform if you need a sanity check.
stages.concept: Spectrum-only reading: carrier position gives $f_p$ directly; sideband spacing gives $2 f_m$; sideband amplitude relative to the carrier gives $m/2$. So $m = 2 \cdot (\text{sideband amp}) / (\text{carrier amp})$. This is exactly what a spectrum analyzer shows a technician debugging an AM transmitter — everything you need is in three peaks.

labels.hidden_peek: waveform hidden — peek to reveal briefly
labels.overmod_desc: envelope inverts — an envelope detector can no longer recover the message
labels.tip1: drag all three sliders; push m past 1
labels.tip3: read spectrum: f_p center, f_m = ½·sideband spacing

1.1: Grab each slider and drag. The top plot is the waveform; the bottom is its spectrum.
1.2: Envelope bumps = f_m cycles per window. Fast oscillations = carrier at f_p. Envelope depth = m.
1.3: Set m above 1 to see over-modulation: the envelope inverts through zero and the signal distorts.

2.1: Count the number of envelope humps to match f_m. The spectrum's sideband spacing = 2·f_m.
2.2: The middle spectrum line is f_p. Slide the carrier until it lands on the target.
2.3: Depth of the envelope = m. At m = 1 the envelope's trough kisses zero.

3.1: Middle line = f_p. Read its label directly.
3.2: Sideband spacing (from one sideband to the next) is 2·f_m. Half it.
3.3: m = 2 × (sideband height) / (carrier height). Read the ratio from the plot.
